title: His-Spin Protein Miniprep
author: Ken Christensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bj48kqzw

steps.title: Prepare column with resin
steps.instruction: Resuspend the His‑Affinity Gel by shaking or vortexing the bottle, then transfer exactly 250 µL of the gel to a Zymo‑Spin P1 column using a 1 mL pipette tip (a 200 µL tip may be too small). Place the column into a collection tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge to collect resin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column for 5–10 seconds until the gel is completely drained; avoid over‑drying the gel by using longer spins.

steps.title: Check sample compatibility
steps.instruction: Ensure the protein sample does not contain >15 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, >10 mM imidazole, EDTA, EGTA, DTT, or excess histidine. If such components are present, dilute the sample with His‑Binding Buffer, adjust pH, imidazole and salt concentrations, or dialyze the sample before loading. For low‑abundance His‑tagged protein requiring >300 µL total, plan to repeat the loading step (see step 4) with up to 300 µL per load. Membrane proteins may be solubilized with up to 2 % non‑ionic detergent (e.g., Triton X‑100 or Tween).

steps.title: Load protein sample onto resin
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL–300 µL of the prepared protein sample to the column, resuspend the gel by shaking or tapping, and incubate for 2 minutes (if the volume exceeds 200 µL, extend the incubation by an additional 1–2 minutes).

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard flow‑through
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column for 5–10 seconds, discard the flow‑through, and return the column to the collection tube.

steps.title: First wash of bound protein
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of His‑Wash Buffer to the resin, resuspend the gel, then centrifuge for 5–10 seconds.

steps.title: Second wash of bound protein
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash step: add another 250 µL of His‑Wash Buffer, resuspend, centrifuge 5–10 seconds, then discard the collection tube.

steps.title: Elute purified protein
steps.instruction: Place the Zymo‑Spin P1 column into a standard microcentrifuge tube, add 150 µL of His‑Elution Buffer (elution volumes of 100–200 µL are acceptable; 150 µL elutes virtually all bound protein), resuspend the gel, and centrifuge for 5–10 seconds to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Post‑purification handling
steps.instruction: The eluate now contains purified protein; use 1–10 µL for SDS‑PAGE and Coomassie staining, and store the remaining protein at an appropriate temperature.

steps.title: Troubleshooting: No protein recovered
steps.instruction: If no protein is recovered, consider that the His‑tag may be inaccessible or the protein insoluble. Purify under denaturing conditions (see step 11) or use a custom elution buffer containing 500 mM imidazole or 100 mM EDTA. Verify the DNA construct for errors.

steps.title: Troubleshooting: Low yield
steps.instruction: If yield is low, lower the imidazole concentration of the His‑Wash Buffer to 25 mM (by diluting with His‑Binding Buffer) or use a custom elution buffer with 500 mM imidazole or 100 mM EDTA.

steps.title: Troubleshooting: Impure eluate
steps.instruction: Check all buffers for contamination and correct pH. Ensure the gel is fully drained after each spin. Add an extra wash step or increase the wash‑buffer imidazole to 60–100 mM (by diluting with His‑Elution Buffer).

steps.title: Denaturing purification (insoluble protein)
steps.instruction:
Prepare denaturing buffers (not supplied):
• Binding buffer: 8 M urea, 10 mM imidazole, 0.1 M sodium phosphate monobasic, 0.01 M Tris, pH 8.0 (adjust with concentrated NaOH).
• Washing buffer: 8 M urea, 50 mM imidazole, 0.1 M sodium phosphate monobasic, 0.01 M Tris, pH 6.3.
• Elution buffer: 8 M urea, 250 mM imidazole, 0.1 M sodium phosphate monobasic, 0.01 M Tris, pH 4.5 (adjust with concentrated HCl).
Urea solutions may shift pH over time; re‑adjust pH before use and store buffers at 4 °C or prepare fresh.
